question: Why must the horn be inspected as part of the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: It indicates whether the vehicle's battery is fully charged
choice_b: It is used to signal other drivers to pass
choice_c: It is a device that must function properly to warn other roadway users of your presence
choice_d: It is required only for vehicles operating at night
explanation: The manual states the horn must function properly in order to warn other roadway users, such as cars, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians, of your presence.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Horn(s)

question: What is required of the windshield during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: It must be clean, with no obstructions except an inspection sticker, and no cracks or flaws
choice_b: It must be replaced if older than five years
choice_c: It only needs to be free of ice in winter months
choice_d: It must have a tint applied for glare reduction
explanation: The manual requires the windshield to be clean with no obstructions except an inspection sticker, and to have no damage such as cracks or flaws to the glass.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: What must you demonstrate when inspecting the wipers and washers?
choice_a: That the washer fluid is a specific brand
choice_b: That the wiper arms and blades are secure and undamaged, and that the washers operate correctly when activated
choice_c: That the wipers can be removed without tools
choice_d: That the wiper blades match the color of the vehicle
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that wiper arms and blades are secure and not damaged, that they operate smoothly, and demonstrating that the windshield washers work correctly by activating them.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Wipers/Washers

question: Why must the heater and defroster be inspected?
choice_a: They control the vehicle's engine temperature gauge
choice_b: They are only relevant for passenger comfort
choice_c: They must be inspected only if the vehicle has air conditioning
choice_d: The defroster improves visibility, especially during cold weather
explanation: The manual explains the defroster improves visibility, especially in cold weather, and requires demonstrating that the heater and defroster work correctly by operating the controls.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Heater/Defroster

question: How do you check that the parking brake will hold the vehicle?
choice_a: Coast downhill with the parking brake engaged
choice_b: Apply the service brake fully and release the parking brake
choice_c: With the parking brake engaged, remove your foot from the service brake and gently pull forward
choice_d: Accelerate hard with the parking brake engaged
explanation: The manual describes the parking brake check as engaging the parking brake, removing your foot from the service brake, and gently pulling forward to inspect that the parking brake holds the vehicle.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: For a combination vehicle, how is the trailer parking brake check performed?
choice_a: By backing up while both brakes are engaged
choice_b: With the parking brake released and the trailer parking brake engaged, remove your foot from the service brake and gently pull forward
choice_c: By disconnecting the trailer and testing it separately
choice_d: With both the parking brake and trailer parking brake released simultaneously
explanation: The manual states the trailer brake check is performed with the parking brake released and the trailer parking brake engaged, removing your foot from the service brake, and gently pulling forward to inspect that the trailer parking brake holds.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: Why must the parking brake function correctly, especially on a grade or hill?
choice_a: It improves the vehicle's fuel efficiency
choice_b: A vehicle allowed to roll could cause damage or injury to other roadway users or property
choice_c: It is only a legal formality with no safety impact
choice_d: It only matters for vehicles parked overnight
explanation: The manual explains the parking brake(s) must function when a vehicle is parked, especially on a grade or hill, because a vehicle allowed to roll could cause damage or injury to other roadway users or property.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: How is the service brake check performed?
choice_a: Accelerate to highway speed and slam on the brakes
choice_b: Test the brakes only while the vehicle is parked
choice_c: Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service (foot) brake, and come to a complete stop, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side
choice_d: Apply only the parking brake while moving
explanation: The manual describes the service brake check as pulling forward at 5 mph, applying the foot brake, and coming to a complete stop while checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side and stops properly.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Service Brake Check

question: What does the service brake check confirm about the vehicle?
choice_a: That the parking brake and service brake are interchangeable
choice_b: That the tires have adequate tread depth
choice_c: That the vehicle can stop from highway speed within 100 feet
choice_d: That the vehicle does not pull to either side and stops properly when the service brake is applied at low speed
explanation: The manual states this procedure is designed to determine that the brakes are working correctly and that the vehicle does not pull to either side at a low speed.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, In-Vehicle/Engine Start - Service Brake Check

question: What happens if you fail to explain and demonstrate all four parts of the air brake check correctly during the CDL Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: You are given a second attempt immediately
choice_b: Only the air brake portion is marked incomplete, with no effect on the overall score
choice_c: You lose 5 points but may still pass
choice_d: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual states that failure to explain and demonstrate all four parts of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake or Hydraulic Brake Check

question: In the first step of the air brake check, to approximately what pressure should the air gauge build after chocking the wheels and starting the vehicle?
choice_a: Approximately 200-250 psi
choice_b: Approximately 20-45 psi
choice_c: Approximately 120-140 psi (governor cutoff)
choice_d: Approximately 55 psi
explanation: The manual states that in the Air Gauge and Governor Cutoff Check, after chocking the wheels and starting the vehicle, you inspect that the air gauge builds air pressure to the governor cutoff, approximately 120-140 psi.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check - Air Gauge and Governor Cutoff Check

question: During the air leakage rate test with the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes versus a combination vehicle?
choice_a: No more than 1 psi for a single vehicle and 2 psi for a combination vehicle
choice_b: There is no maximum; any drop is acceptable if the buzzer does not sound
choice_c: No more than 10 psi for either vehicle type
choice_d: No more than 3 psi in one minute for a single vehicle, and no more than 4 psi in one minute for a combination vehicle
explanation: The manual states the air pressure should not drop more than 3 pounds in one minute for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes, or 4 pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check - Air Leakage Rate Test

question: Before what air pressure level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) activate?
choice_a: Only after the engine has been shut off for ten minutes
choice_b: Before air pressure drops below 20 psi
choice_c: Before air pressure drops below 55 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer
choice_d: Before air pressure drops below 100 psi
explanation: The manual states the low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer, and it is the applicant's responsibility to know the manufacturer's specifications.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check - Air Warning Device(s) Test

topic: Air Brake Check - Emergency Brake Test
question: Between what pressure range should the parking (or emergency) brake valve close (pop out) during the emergency brake test?
choice_a: Between 55 psi and 70 psi
choice_b: Between 100 psi and 120 psi
choice_c: Between 20 psi and 45 psi
choice_d: Between 0 psi and 10 psi
explanation: The manual states the parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi, no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check - Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: What must you do at the very start of the air brake check before building air pressure?
choice_a: Disconnect the trailer
choice_b: Remove the wheel entirely
choice_c: Chock the wheels and start the vehicle
choice_d: Drain all air from the system first
explanation: The manual's first step in the air brake check is to chock the wheels, start the vehicle, and inspect that the air gauge is working and builds pressure to governor cutoff.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check - Air Gauge and Governor Cutoff Check

question: With the transmission in "park," how is the hydraulic brake pedal pressure typically inspected?
choice_a: Tap the pedal ten times rapidly
choice_b: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds, or as specified by the manufacturer
choice_c: Press the pedal once and immediately release it
choice_d: Hold the pedal down for one full minute continuously
explanation: The manual describes inspecting brake pedal pressure by pumping the brake pedal three times and then holding it down for five seconds, or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: After the initial application during the hydraulic brake pedal check, what should the brake pedal NOT do?
choice_a: It should bounce back up immediately
choice_b: It should not move (depress) further and should remain firm with reserve pressure
choice_c: It should feel spongy but recover after release
choice_d: It should slowly sink to the floor over several seconds
explanation: The manual states the brake pedal should not move (depress) after initial application and should be firm with a sufficient amount of reserve for brake pedal application.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What is the consequence of failing to correctly explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: A warning, with a chance to redo the check once
choice_b: No consequence, since it is optional for hydraulic-brake vehicles
choice_c: A deduction of only two points from the total score
choice_d: An automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual states that failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What must you inspect about bus entry doors used for normal entry or exit?
choice_a: That they are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside
choice_b: That they lock automatically when the bus reaches highway speed
choice_c: That they open only from the outside
choice_d: That they are painted the same color as the bus body
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that entry doors are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside, since all passengers must be able to enter and exit safely.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Passenger and School Bus Only - Passenger Entry and Lift

question: How many emergency exits must you demonstrate operate smoothly and close securely during the inspection?
choice_a: Exactly two, one on each side of the vehicle
choice_b: All emergency exits on the vehicle
choice_c: At least one, while pointing out and describing how all other emergency exits operate
choice_d: None; emergency exits are visually inspected only
explanation: The manual requires demonstrating that at least one emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, and is not damaged, while pointing out and describing how all other emergency exits operate.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Passenger and School Bus Only - Emergency Exits

question: What must be inspected regarding passenger seats and frames?
choice_a: That seat cushions match in color
choice_b: That all seats recline to the same angle
choice_c: That there are no broken seat frames and that frames are firmly attached to the floor
choice_d: That seats are removable for cargo space
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that there are no broken seat frames, that seat frames are firmly attached to the floor, and that seat cushions are attached securely to the frames.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Passenger and School Bus Only - Passenger Seating

question: What is inspected regarding passenger mirrors and monitoring devices, if equipped?
choice_a: That they are removed before the inspection begins
choice_b: That they are clean, viewable from the inside, and the video display is operable and adjusted for viewing
choice_c: That they are painted to match the bus interior
choice_d: That they are only checked once per year by a mechanic
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that passenger monitoring devices or cameras, if equipped, are clean and viewable from the inside with the video display operable and adjusted for viewing.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Passenger and School Bus Only - Passenger Monitoring Devices

question: Which student lights must be inspected and demonstrated on both the front and back of a school bus?
choice_a: Only the headlights and taillights
choice_b: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
choice_c: Only the stop arm light
choice_d: Interior dome lights only
explanation: The manual requires inspecting and demonstrating the strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights, on both the front and back of the school bus, along with their dash indicators.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, School Bus Only - Student Lights

question: What is the purpose of the stop arm on a school bus?
choice_a: It warns other drivers that a school bus is stopping or is stopped
choice_b: It signals the driver to check mirrors
choice_c: It forces students to cross well away from the front of the bus
choice_d: It automatically applies the parking brake
explanation: The manual states the stop arm warns other drivers that a school bus is stopping or is stopped, while the separate safety arm forces students to cross well away from the front of the bus in the driver's view.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, School Bus Only - Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: What is the purpose of the safety arm on a school bus?
choice_a: It measures the distance to the vehicle behind
choice_b: It automatically opens the entry door
choice_c: It forces students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the bus in the driver's view
choice_d: It warns other drivers the bus is stopping
explanation: The manual states the safety arm forces school students to cross well, for example 10 feet, away from the front of the school bus in the driver's view.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, School Bus Only - Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: Which lights must be inspected during the Lights Operations Check on all vehicles?
choice_a: Interior dome lights and dashboard illumination only
choice_b: Only the headlights
choice_c: Only the brake lights and turn signals
choice_d: Left and right turn signals, 4-way flashers, low and high beam headlights, clearance or marker lights, taillights, and brake lights
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that all lights operate and illuminate, including left and right turn signals, 4-way flashers, low beam headlights, high beam headlights, clearance or marker lights, taillights, and brake lights.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Lights Operations Check

question: What must brake lights do when the brakes are applied and released?
choice_a: Come "on" when brakes are applied and turn "off" when brakes are released
choice_b: Only illuminate at night
choice_c: Stay on continuously regardless of brake application
choice_d: Flash rapidly whenever the vehicle is in motion
explanation: The manual specifically requires inspecting that brake lights come on when brakes are applied and turn off when brakes are released.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Lights Operations Check

question: How must the operation of all external lights be inspected?
choice_a: From outside the vehicle, directing the examiner while activating the lights from inside
choice_b: Using a mirror held up to the vehicle's rear
choice_c: External lights are not part of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_d: From inside the vehicle only, using the dashboard indicators
explanation: The manual states the operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle, and you must direct the examiner to the front, sides, and rear as you activate the lights from inside and speak loud enough to be heard.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Lights Operations Check

question: What condition must the front light lenses or covers be in?
choice_a: Removable for easy cleaning
choice_b: Made of the same material as the windshield
choice_c: The proper color, clean, not broken and not missing
choice_d: Tinted for glare reduction
explanation: The manual states light lenses or covers must be clean and free of damage for the lights to work properly, and must be the proper color, clean, not broken, and not missing.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Front of Vehicle/Engine Area - Lenses

question: With the engine off, which four fluid levels should you inspect in the engine area?
choice_a: Only engine oil and windshield washer fluid
choice_b: Fuel level and tire inflation only
choice_c: Engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only)
choice_d: Transmission fluid and windshield washer fluid
explanation: The manual instructs inspecting, with the engine off, the engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only) for proper levels between the add and full marks.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Front of Vehicle/Engine Area - Critical Fluid Levels

question: What should you look for when inspecting for fluid and air leaks under the vehicle?
choice_a: The vehicle's registration sticker
choice_b: Only the color of the exhaust smoke
choice_c: Tire tread wear patterns
choice_d: Puddles on the ground and dripping fluids around and on the underside of the engine and transmission
explanation: The manual instructs looking for puddles on the ground and dripping fluids around and on the underside of the engine and transmission, and inspecting hoses and air lines for condition and leaks.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Front of Vehicle/Engine Area - Fluid and Air Leaks

question: Besides checking that the power steering box is securely mounted and not leaking, what else must be inspected on the steering system?
choice_a: That the steering wheel diameter meets a minimum size
choice_b: That there are no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys, and that linkage joints and sockets are not worn or loose
choice_c: That the steering wheel is a specific color
choice_d: That the horn button is centered on the steering wheel
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the steering system has no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys, and that visible connecting links, arms, rods, joints, and sockets are not worn, cracked, or loose.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Front of Vehicle/Engine Area - Steering System

question: How should you check tire inflation during a vehicle inspection?
choice_a: By visually estimating the tire's roundness
choice_b: By listening for a hissing sound only
choice_c: By kicking each tire firmly
choice_d: Using a tire gauge; you will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet
explanation: The manual explicitly notes that you must mention the use of a tire gauge and will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet to check inflation.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required in major grooves containing wear bars for steering axle tires versus other tires?
choice_a: 2/32 inch on steering axle tires and 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_b: 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires
choice_c: 6/32 inch on all tires regardless of position
choice_d: 1/32 inch on steering axle tires and 3/32 inch on other tires
explanation: The manual specifies inspecting for minimum tread depth with a tread depth gauge on all major tread grooves containing wear bars: 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Tires

question: What should you inspect for regarding tire condition beyond inflation and tread depth?
choice_a: Whether the tire matches the vehicle's paint color
choice_b: The manufacturer's logo visibility
choice_c: The exact date of manufacture only
choice_d: Cuts and damage exposing body plies, missing valve caps, damaged valve stems, and bumps or bulges in the sidewall
explanation: The manual requires inspecting tire condition for cuts and damage that expose body plies in the tread and sidewall, missing valve caps, damaged or broken valve stems, and bumps, bulges, or mismatched dual tire diameters.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Tires

question: What repair is NOT allowed on a damaged rim, according to the manual?
choice_a: Replacing the entire rim
choice_b: Re-torquing the lug nuts
choice_c: Welding repairs
choice_d: Cleaning rust from the rim surface
explanation: The manual states that rims cannot have welding repairs, and you should inspect for damaged, cracked, or bent rims and for rust trails that may indicate a rim is loose on a wedge wheel.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Rims/Wheels

question: What sign on the lug nuts might indicate they are loose?
choice_a: A dull, matte finish
choice_b: Uniform torque marks
choice_c: Slight discoloration from heat only
choice_d: Rust trails or shiny threads
explanation: The manual states that lug nuts should be inspected to confirm they are not loose, and that rust trails or shiny threads may show looseness.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Wheel Fasteners (Lug Nuts)

question: What can result from damaged or missing leaf springs, according to the manual?
choice_a: Improved fuel economy
choice_b: A smoother ride with no safety impact
choice_c: Loss of control or rollover if the vehicle falls on the frame or on a tire
choice_d: Faster acceleration
explanation: The manual explains that damaged or missing leaf springs or coils may lead to loss of control or rollover if the vehicle falls on the frame or on a tire.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Springs and Air Bags and Shocks

question: As part of the springs and suspension inspection, what should you check about how the vehicle is sitting?
choice_a: That the cab is higher than the trailer
choice_b: That the vehicle leans to the driver's side
choice_c: That the vehicle is tilted slightly forward
choice_d: That the vehicle is sitting level, front to rear and side to side
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the vehicle is sitting level, front to rear and side to side, and notes a leaning vehicle may indicate a suspension problem.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Springs and Air Bags and Shocks

question: What should you inspect regarding brake hoses or lines?
choice_a: That they are painted a specific color for easy identification
choice_b: That they can supply air or hydraulic fluid without leaking, and are not cracked, worn, or frayed
choice_c: That they are made of rubber only, never metal
choice_d: That they are the shortest possible length
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that hoses or lines can supply air or hydraulic fluid to the brakes without leaking, checking for cracked, worn, or frayed hoses or lines, and secure couplings and fittings.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Brake Lines / Hoses / Leaks

question: What is inspected when checking for brake contaminates?
choice_a: The manufacturer's part number stamped on the brake pad
choice_b: The temperature of the brake drum after a long drive
choice_c: Whether contaminants such as grease or oil are present on the brake lining or pads and the brake drum or disc
choice_d: The color of the brake fluid only
explanation: The manual states that if accessible, you should inspect for contaminants such as grease or oil on the brake lining or pads and the brake drum or disc that can affect braking capabilities.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Steering Axle - Brake Contaminates

question: What condition must side light lenses and reflectors be in?
choice_a: Only inspected if the vehicle is over ten years old
choice_b: Tinted to match the vehicle's paint
choice_c: The proper color, clean, not broken or missing
choice_d: Removable without tools
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that light lenses or covers and reflectors on the sides of the vehicle and trailer are the proper color, clean, and not broken or missing.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Side of Vehicle - Lenses and Reflectors

topic: Side Mirrors and Traffic Monitoring Devices
question: What must be inspected about the side view mirrors?
choice_a: That they are the same size on both sides
choice_b: That they are clean, not cracked, and mirror brackets are not bent and are mounted securely with no missing parts
choice_c: That they fold in automatically at highway speed
choice_d: That they are tinted for glare reduction
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that mirrors are clean and not cracked, and that mirror brackets are not bent and are mounted securely with no missing parts.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Side of Vehicle - Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: What is a sign of a problem with the battery connections during inspection?
choice_a: Excessive corrosion at the connections
choice_b: A secure battery box cover
choice_c: A fully charged battery gauge reading
choice_d: New-looking cables
explanation: The manual states that all connections should be tight and should not show signs of excessive corrosion, if visible, and that batteries should be secure with cables not cracked or worn.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Side of Vehicle - Battery/Electrical System

question: What must be inspected regarding fuel tanks, including Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tanks if equipped?
choice_a: That they are painted a reflective color
choice_b: That they include a built-in fire extinguisher
choice_c: That they are securely mounted, caps are tight, and there are no leaks from tanks or lines
choice_d: That they are filled to exactly 100% capacity
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that all fuel tanks, including DEF tanks if equipped, are securely mounted, caps are tight, and there are no leaks from tanks or lines, since leaks are a fire hazard.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Side of Vehicle - Fuel Tank(s)

question: What could result from loose or cracked frame members, according to the manual?
choice_a: No effect unless the frame is completely severed
choice_b: Reduced vehicle stability, causing handling and cornering problems such as wandering or possible rollover
choice_c: Improved ride comfort
choice_d: Increased cargo capacity
explanation: The manual explains that loose or cracked frame members may reduce vehicle stability, causing handling and cornering problems such as wandering and possible rollover, resulting in total loss of vehicle control.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Side of Vehicle - Frame(s)

question: On a combination vehicle, which part of the vehicle's rear lenses and reflectors do you need to inspect?
choice_a: Both the tractor and trailer rears equally
choice_b: Neither; rear lenses are optional on combination vehicles
choice_c: Only the rear of the trailer
choice_d: Only the rear of the power unit/tractor
explanation: The manual notes that on a combination vehicle, you need only inspect the rear of the trailer for lenses and reflectors that must be the proper color, clean, and not broken or missing.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Rear of Vehicle or Trailer - Lenses and Reflectors

question: What must be inspected about the air and electric connectors between the power unit and trailer?
choice_a: Only the connectors on the power unit, not the trailer
choice_b: That they are seated and sealed, free of damage, and locked into place on both the power unit and the trailer
choice_c: That they are disconnected before every trip
choice_d: Only that they are the same brand as the tractor
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that air and electric connectors on both the power unit and trailer are seated and sealed, free of damage, and locked into place, and notes you must inspect connections on both to receive credit.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines / Connectors

question: What must be inspected about the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: That it matches the trailer manufacturer
choice_b: That it is removable for cleaning between trips
choice_c: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform, and inspected for cracks, breaks, or excessive wear
choice_d: That it is painted a bright color for visibility
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the fifth wheel skid plate is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform, checking for cracks, breaks, or excessive wear, and proper lubrication if applicable.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Fifth Wheel Combinations Only - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

question: What should you check regarding the fit between the trailer apron and the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: That the apron is intentionally raised off the skid plate
choice_b: That there is a visible half-inch gap for proper airflow
choice_c: That the kingpin is loosely seated for easy release
choice_d: That the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap between the apron and the fifth wheel
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate and that there is no space (gap) between the apron and the fifth wheel.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Fifth Wheel Combinations Only - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: What must be inspected about the pintle hook on a pintle hook combination?
choice_a: That it opens automatically when reversing
choice_b: That it is coated in a rust-proof paint
choice_c: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame with no loose or missing parts, cracks, breaks, or excessive wear
choice_d: That it is the same weight as the trailer drawbar
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the pintle hook is securely mounted to the vehicle frame, checking for loose or missing mounting bolts, nuts, pins, brackets, and clamps, and for cracks, breaks, or excessive wear.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Pintle Hook Combinations Only - Pintle Hook

question: For a fifth wheel coupling system, what must you inspect inside the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin, with no play between the kingpin and locking jaws/lever
choice_b: That the kingpin has been removed for storage
choice_c: That the gap is filled with grease
choice_d: That the release arm is disengaged
explanation: The manual requires looking into the fifth wheel gap and inspecting that locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin, with no play, and that the release arm is in the engaged position with the safety latch or lock in place.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Combination Vehicles Only - Locking and Safety Devices

question: What should you inspect about the trailer coupler and tongue on non-fifth-wheel combinations?
choice_a: That the coupler is welded shut for extra security
choice_b: That the coupler is not bent or twisted, is secured to the tongue with no loose or missing bolts, and the tongue has no dents, twists, cracks, or broken welds
choice_c: That the tongue is fully retractable
choice_d: That the coupler color matches the trailer body
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the trailer coupler is not bent or twisted, is secured to the tongue with no loose or missing bolts or broken welds, and that the tongue can support the weight of the load without dents, twists, cracks, or broken welds.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, All Other Types of Combinations - Trailer Coupler & Tongue

question: What must be inspected about the trailer's landing gear?
choice_a: That it is fully lowered while driving for stability
choice_b: That it is removed entirely for lighter towing
choice_c: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged
choice_d: That it is painted a bright warning color
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged, since damage could cause the trailer to tip when disconnected.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, Trailers Only - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: What is required regarding reflective tape on trailers, per the manual?
choice_a: It is required on tractors but not trailers
choice_b: It must be replaced every six months regardless of condition
choice_c: It must be present and affixed securely on the sides and rear of the trailer, if required
choice_d: It is only decorative and has no inspection requirement
explanation: The manual states that reflective tape on the sides and rear of the trailer must be present and affixed securely, allowing the driver of a commercial vehicle to be seen and to communicate presence with other traffic; it is only required for trailers.
